title: Container Administration Command
description: An adversary uses a container administration service (the Kubernetes API server, kubelet, Docker daemon, or an in-cluster admission proxy) to execute a command inside a running container. The canonical surface is `kubectl exec` / `oc exec` / Kubernetes API `POST /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{pod}/exec`, and equivalents on the kubelet (`/exec`, `/run`) and on Docker (`docker exec`). Detection is anchored on the API audit trail and on the resulting in-container process lineage.

microsoft_k8s_matrix.name: Exec into container
microsoft_k8s_matrix.description: Adversaries with permissions on the Kubernetes API can run commands in a running container via `kubectl exec`, bypassing image-level controls and admission policies that gate pod creation.

data_components.name: Application Log Content
data_components.definition: Logs generated by an application or service, in this matrix scoped to the Kubernetes API server audit log and the kubelet log. The exec verb against the pods/exec subresource is the highest-fidelity signal for T1609.
relevant_events: Kubernetes audit event: verb=create, objectRef.resource=pods, objectRef.subresource=exec
Kubernetes audit event: verb=create, objectRef.resource=pods, objectRef.subresource=attach
kubelet log entry for /exec and /run handlers
Direct kubelet exec endpoint: POST to kubelet TCP/10250 at path /exec or /run (bypasses API server audit when kubelet is reachable directly)

data_components.name: Command Execution
data_components.definition: The execution of a command, including arguments, parent process, and invoking principal. For T1609 this surfaces as the command run inside the target container and as the kubectl/docker invocation on the operator side.
relevant_events: Container process command line captured by an in-cluster runtime sensor (eBPF, Falco, Sysdig)
kubectl/docker client command line on a workstation or CI runner

data_components.name: Process Creation
data_components.definition: The creation of a new process. For T1609 the signal is a process born inside a container whose ancestry traces to the runtime's exec helper (containerd-shim, runc init, dockerd-exec) rather than to the container's PID 1 entrypoint.
relevant_events: Process exec event with parent=runc or parent=containerd-shim and pid_namespace==target_container
EDR process tree showing shell/binary launched outside the documented entrypoint chain

data_components.name: Container Modification
data_components.definition: Modification of an existing workload's pod template via a patch operation against Deployment, DaemonSet, or StatefulSet resources to inject a sidecar container. This is a second execution path for T1609 alongside direct exec, tagged T1609 by SigmaHQ community rules. The new container starts on next pod replacement and runs adversary code in the same pod network/PID namespace as the legitimate container.
relevant_events: Kubernetes audit event: verb=patch, apiGroup=apps, objectRef.resource in {deployments, daemonsets, statefulsets}, requestObject.spec.template.spec.containers includes a container not present in the previous revision
New container appearing in a running pod's spec that was not present at original pod creation

data_components.name: Network Traffic Content
data_components.definition: Application-layer content of network traffic. For T1609 this is the SPDY/WebSocket-upgraded HTTPS stream from the API server to the kubelet that carries the exec session, and the stream from a client to the API server.
relevant_events: HTTPS request to API server path matching /api/v1/namespaces/*/pods/*/exec
Sustained WebSocket / SPDY upgrade stream from API server to kubelet on TCP/10250

detection_strategies.name: Detection Strategy for Container Administration Command Abuse
detection_strategies.summary: Correlate Kubernetes API audit events for the pods/exec subresource with the resulting process creation inside the targeted container. The API event carries who and where; the in-container process event carries what.

detection_strategies.name: Anomalous use of management utilities
detection_strategies.summary: Flag use of `docker exec` and `kubectl exec` that is not produced by a known automation principal (CI service account, GitOps controller, paved-road operator console), correlated with unexpected process creation inside the container.

vendor_detections.title: Kubernetes API exec by non-allowlisted principal
vendor_detections.intent: Surface every Kubernetes audit event where a principal created an exec or attach subresource against a pod, excluding a small allowlist of automation identities.
vendor_detections.query:
// Wiz Threat Center / Kubernetes Audit Log query (Resource Graph style)
KubernetesAuditLog
| where verb == "create"
  and objectRef.resource == "pods"
  and objectRef.subresource in ("exec", "attach")
| where user.username !in~ (
    "system:serviceaccount:argocd:argocd-application-controller",
    "system:serviceaccount:flux-system:source-controller",
    "system:serviceaccount:tekton-pipelines:tekton-pipelines-controller"
  )
| project requestReceivedTimestamp,
          principal = user.username,
          sourceIPs,
          namespace = objectRef.namespace,
          pod = objectRef.name,
          container = requestObject.container,
          command = requestObject.command,
          userAgent
required_telemetry: Wiz Kubernetes audit log connector enabled on each cluster
API server audit policy with Metadata level (or higher) on pods/exec
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: Break-glass operators and incident responders will appear here. Maintain the allowlist as an enum, not a literal list inline.
vendor_detections.limitations: Does not see the command actually run inside the container if the audit policy does not capture requestObject for exec. Pair with a runtime-level rule for that.

vendor_detections.title: Upwind Explorer: process born under runc/containerd-shim outside entrypoint chain
vendor_detections.intent: Detect a process executing inside a container whose parent is the runtime's exec helper rather than the container's documented entrypoint, indicating a remote exec session opened the process. Authored as a Rego policy for Upwind Explorer, the documented custom-detection path.
vendor_detections.query:
package upwind.detections.t1609.container_admin_exec_runtime_signal

# Detects an exec session into a running container by matching the process
# ancestry signature: parent is the runtime's exec helper (runc / containerd-
# shim / dockerd) rather than the container's documented entrypoint chain.
#
# Input shape follows the Upwind Explorer process_exec event, parameterized
# below. Field paths (input.process.parent.name, input.identity.k8s_user)
# follow the public Explorer documentation pattern; verify against your
# tenant's actual schema before deploying.

default deny := false

runtime_exec_helpers := {
  "runc",
  "containerd-shim-runc-v2",
  "dockerd",
  "docker-runc",
}

ignored_child_names := {"pause"}

deny if {
  input.event.kind == "process_exec"
  input.container.id != ""
  input.process.parent.name in runtime_exec_helpers
  contains(input.process.parent.args, "exec")
  not input.process.name in ignored_child_names
}

finding := {
  "severity": "high",
  "technique": "T1609",
  "cluster": input.cluster.name,
  "namespace": input.workload.namespace,
  "workload": input.workload.name,
  "image": input.container.image,
  "process": input.process.cmdline,
  "parent": input.process.parent.cmdline,
  "k8s_user": input.identity.k8s_user,
  "k8s_serviceaccount": input.identity.k8s_serviceaccount,
} if {
  deny
}
required_telemetry: Upwind sensor (eBPF DaemonSet) deployed on every node
Upwind Kubernetes audit log enrichment enabled so process events carry the originating API principal (input.identity.k8s_user / k8s_serviceaccount)
Upwind Explorer custom-policy authoring access for the tenant
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: Liveness/readiness probes that shell into the container are legitimate exec ancestry. Allowlist by kubelet probe principal or by container-and-cmdline pair, not by process name.
vendor_detections.limitations: Authoring custom Rego policies against Upwind Explorer requires access to Upwind's documentation center, which is login-gated. The field names above follow public marketing/blog references and may need adjustment against the actual tenant schema.

vendor_detections.title: Audit-log-anchored exec hunt over the K8s lake
vendor_detections.intent: Hunt over centralized Kubernetes audit logs in the data lake for exec/attach events that are not produced by a known automation principal, with a 7-day baseline.
vendor_detections.query:
-- Assumes K8S_AUDIT.PUBLIC.EVENTS is the normalized audit-log landing table.
-- Constants are kept in a side table so business code stays literal-free.
WITH
  allowlist AS (
    SELECT principal
    FROM   K8S_AUDIT.REF.EXEC_PRINCIPAL_ALLOWLIST
  ),
  exec_events AS (
    SELECT
        event_time,
        cluster_name,
        user_username      AS principal,
        source_ips,
        object_namespace   AS namespace,
        object_name        AS pod,
        request_object:container::string AS container,
        request_object:command          AS command,
        user_agent
    FROM K8S_AUDIT.PUBLIC.EVENTS
    WHERE verb = 'create'
      AND object_resource    = 'pods'
      AND object_subresource IN ('exec', 'attach')
      AND event_time >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
  )
SELECT *
FROM   exec_events
WHERE  principal NOT IN (SELECT principal FROM allowlist)
ORDER  BY event_time DESC;
required_telemetry: Kubernetes audit logs shipped to Snowflake (e.g., via Fluent Bit -> S3 -> Snowpipe)
K8S_AUDIT.REF.EXEC_PRINCIPAL_ALLOWLIST reference table populated and reviewed quarterly
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: Latency between event and table can mask live incidents; pair with a streaming alerting tier for time-sensitive use.
vendor_detections.limitations: Sees only what made it into the audit policy; does not see in-container process events unless a runtime sensor's events are also landed in the lake.
